scope: Functional PRACTICAL-GOAL kernel/apps and actual compute-C retirement into Rust plus reviewed assembly; deferred qualification remains deferred.
source_conclusions: C changes only select existing CPU_HELPERS ABI forwarding and remove the selected default shim/declaration after all its C callers move. Original fallback computation is retained; no new compute-C behavior.

clear receives the actual embedded CPU-local idle Thread through C, requires it nonnull as before, and selects saved/default using the existing ABI fp_regs field. It adds no Thread mutation, allocation, free or scheduler operation. Existing CPU/IRQ exclusion and pointer lifetimes remain caller requirements.

Signal reset preserves nonzero availability semantics, unavailable-initial -95 with no lookup/restore, one native_xrstor_checked call on the available path, full unsigned64 mask and exact signed64 result. Only the no-XSAVE path calls the real existing current bridge before the unchanged Rust default body; NULL current remains supported by that body.

FXSAVE helper uses actual repr(C,align16) I387FxsaveStruct with compile-time size512/align16/offset28 assertions. MaybeUninit reserves the full write extent and only the initialized u32 mask is read. General inline-asm memory effects are retained; nostack and preserves_flags fit FXSAVE. Nonzero SSE selection executes one FXSAVE; SSE0 and zero masks return 0xffbf.

Retained native object independently disassembled: one FXSAVE through a 512-byte stack allocation, offset28 u32 mask load, no incidental SIMD. Stack alignment uses established SysV call-stack alignment; production no-redzone/no-SIMD profile must remain.

CMake selects native Rust cfg, native signal C macro and existing fault assembly under the same linux-6.12 profile. Legacy cfg keeps clear without signal exports or checked-XRSTOR import. Four strict combined selected C boundaries use actual contiguous candidate selection and no unused-function suppression.
